Capacity factor example - interpret utilization
1 Maximum annual energy
(100 MW)(8760 h) = 876,000 MWh.
2 Capacity factor
CF = 438,000

For a 100 MW unit, a 50% capacity factor means an average output of 50 MW over the
period, regardless of the exact run-time pattern.

Planning example - identify the capacity gap
Wildcatland forecasts a peak demand of
4380 MW, has 4850 MW of accredited planning
capacity, and uses a 15% target PRM. Does
the system meet the target, and what is the
capacity gap?
Compare accredited planning capacity with the PRM-based target, not with annual
generation.

ECE 685 | Optimal Fuel Mix I 21/33

LDC construction
1 Validate the source profile : confirm interval length, units, missing values, and
covered time.
2 Sort demand in descending order : retain every value; change only its
position.
3 Assign duration: for equal blocks, each rank adds the same Δ𝑡.
4 Verify invariants: peak, minimum, duration, and area must match the
chronological record.
The chronological profile remains the source data. The LDC is a derived view.
